claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child I'd like to claim for - their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! It's lovely to hear from you, and I'm happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Next, could you tell me if Alex lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since Alex doesn't live with you, could you tell me if you contribute towards the cost of looking after Alex? For example, do you pay for things like their food, clothing, or other living expenses, and if so, is this at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards Alex's needs - things like clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing. I pay a bit over £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Could you tell me who Alex lives with? For example, do they live with your partner, another family member, or someone else? And is that person already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with my ex-partner, but no, they're not claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the picture:

Is Alex in full-time education or training, and are they a British citizen or do they have the right to live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 13, so yes, they're in school - just regular secondary school. And yes, Alex has the right to live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Now I just need to ask a couple of questions about your own circumstances:

Are you aged 16 or over, and do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm over 16, but actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions about your situation:

1. Are you working abroad for the UK government, or are you a member of the UK armed forces posted overseas?

Or alternatively, do you work in another country but pay National Insurance contributions in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of those apply to me. I'm not working for the UK government or in the armed forces, and I'm not paying National Insurance contributions in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Residency requirement not met:** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to live in the UK. While there are exceptions for people living abroad (such as those working for the UK government, serving in the UK armed forces overseas, or working in another country while paying UK National Insurance contributions), you've confirmed that none of these apply to your situation.

**What you do meet:**
- Alex is under 16 and in full-time education ✓
- Alex has the right to live in the UK ✓
- You contribute financially towards Alex's care at a rate exceeding the Child Benefit amount ✓

However, because you don't currently live in the UK and don't meet any of the exceptions for claiming from abroad, you would not be eligible at this time.

**If your circumstances change** (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you may become eligible to claim. Additionally, Alex's other parent (your ex-partner) may be eligible to claim Child Benefit if they meet the criteria, as Alex lives with them.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?

Although the claimant contributes financially to Alex's care (over £26 per week, which exceeds the Child Benefit rate), and Alex is under 16, in full-time education, and has the right to live in the UK, the claimant's residency outside the UK without meeting any of the special exceptions means they are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

While other conditions regarding the child are met - Alex is under 16, in education, has the right to live in the UK, and the claimant contributes financially - the residency requirement for the claimant is not satisfied.
